controls: Gate the RVV path with the same compile/runtime SIMD gate used by the rest of faiss (COMPILE_SIMD_RISCV_RVV / SIMDConfig) and keep the scalar NONE base for comparison and fallback
Choose clamp instructions to exactly match the scalar compare semantics, or use vmerge from vmflt/vmfgt masks; verify NaN and ±0 behavior on hardware/simulator
Add an explicit lane-independent shortcut for vdiff==0 written once before the strip-mine loop
Benchmark d sweep (e.g. 4..512) and pick LMUL and a short-input threshold on the target core; do not hard-code a lane count
Compile-check the RVV path and re-verify the ELF attributes include v; confirm the symbol instantiates the new path via disassembly
A/B validate error by comparing vector vs scalar encode bit-for-bit before switching
reasons: RVV elementwise FP ops must reproduce the scalar per-lane roundings: replacing fdiv.s then fmul.s by a single precomputed reciprocal multiply can change low-order bits and recons error
vfmin/vfmax NaN and signed-zero semantics differ from the branchy scalar clamp; the reference clamp must win on special values
vdiff==0 must map every lane to 0 exactly; a per-lane test inside the vector body would be wrong
dynamic-tail and vsetvl/v set up add overhead that can regress very short vectors (small d)
reachability risk: adding intrinsics to the header/cpp without keeping the NONE fallback compiled can leave non-RVV platforms broken or the realized path unreachable
fusing *255 into the scale constant changes error vs the reference (fdiv then mul), so it must be validated even if faster

conditions.description: libfaiss.so stays built with COMPILE_SIMD_RISCV_RVV and vector caps v1p0/zve32f/zvl128b as shown in the ELF attribute string
target hardware exposes RVV v; verify VLEN via vlenb before tuning LMUL
encode semantics to preserve elementwise: code[i]=(int)(255*clamp((x[i]-vmin)/vdiff,0,1)) with all-zero code when vdiff==0
the RISCV_RVV QuantizerTemplate marker specializations are replaced by a real encode path reachable from sq_dispatch
bit-exactness or the project's explicit tolerance contract for 8-bit SQ output is respected (sq-accuracy keeps sql2_recons_error stable and ndiff_for_idempotence 0)

actions.proposal: Implement a real RVV encode_vector for the QT_8bit (Codec8bit<RISCV_RVV>) QuantizerTemplate in sq-rvv.cpp instead of inheriting the scalar NONE base: precompute scalar invariants (vmin, vdiff, and 255/vdiff reciprocal, plus the vdiff==0 shortcut) before the loop, then strip-mine over d with dynamic __riscv_vsetvl, vle32 unit-stride loads of x, vfsub.vf vmin, vfmul.vf (or vfdiv.vv) scale, two-sided clamp via vfmin/vfmax (or compare+mask-merge to match the reference's NaN/signed-zero behavior), vfcvt.rtz.xu.f.v and vfncvt narrowing to uint8, then vse8 stores; keep the existing scalar implementation for non-RVV builds and for a short-input tail.

correctness_checks: Compare encode_vector output byte-for-byte between scalar NONE base and the new RVV path over uniform and random float inputs plus NaN/±0/±Inf/subnormals and vdiff==0 at the benchmark's d range; expect bit equality if the same IEEE op sequence is retained, else within documented tolerance
Re-run the sq-accuracy benchmark and assert benchmark_QT_8bit_sql2_recons_error and benchmark_QT_8bit_ndiff_for_idempotence remain identical to baseline
Verify tail handling for d%VL!=0 and d==0, and a d smaller than VLMAX
Run under an RVV-disabled build (or a hardware-implementation check) to confirm the scalar fallback still returns identical codes and no illegal instruction traps

a short-input scalar/tail path (and its d-threshold branch) appears if introduced to guard small vectors

controls: Take const local copies of d/vmin/vdiff exactly once before the loop and keep loop writes restricted to code[] only
Use the existing caller guarantee that codes come from separately allocated code buffers; document the no-alias precondition
Compare outputs of the stopgap against the pre-change build during transition
Drop this change when the RVV encode_vector replaces the loop
reasons: Hoisting this->d/vdiff assumes the members do not change mid-loop; if code or x aliased *this the reloads were semantically required
Pointer end arithmetic could overflow for pathological d; the real benchmark d is small but must be proven at each call site
If RVV encode lands, this scalar-only repair is throwaway work and could diverge from the vector path's output if implemented inconsistently
Compiler may still re-materialize loads if it cannot prove no aliasing through the uint8_t store even with locals (lower benefit than expected; still removes the this-> reloads)

conditions.description: Apply on the scalar fallback path only, as a stopgap before RVV encode_vector lands
Caller contract guarantees code/x do not alias *this (fresh encode buffers), so hoisting member loads is safe; verify at call sites
d is small enough that code_end=code+d does not overflow the address space

actions.proposal: For the scalar NONE encode_vector (the path currently used by the RISCV_RVV fallback), copy this->d, this->vmin, and this->vdiff into const locals before the loop and express the traversal with pointer increments (code pointer += 1, x pointer += 1) plus a precomputed end pointer (code_end = code + d), so the per-iteration ld a4,8(a0), flw fa4,20(a0), and add a3,a2,a5 no longer execute; if the RVV encode lands, fold this in and delete the scalar-only fix.

correctness_checks: Bit-identical encode results across the full sq-accuracy benchmark input set (ndiff_for_idempotence stays 0)
Edge cases d==0 and d==1 behave identically (zero iterations; single component)
Verify at least one call site that code buffers can alias anything is absent, otherwise fall back to non-hoisted iteration

a prologue with register-held d (end pointer) and hoisted vmin/vdiff appears before the loop

gaps.description: Hardware ISA exposure (RVV v availability, actual VLEN via vlenb, core model) is not verified on the run host; only the build ISA from the libfaiss.so ELF attribute string (v1p0, zvl128b, zve64d) is known.

The sq-accuracy benchmark workload (dimension d, vector count, and which call sites drive encode_vector for QT_8bit) was not inspected; the faiss/tests source lookup returned source_missing, and only benchmark CSV metrics (benchmark_QT_8bit_* values) are available.
No vectorized encode implementation exists to measure, so the speedup benefit of the RVV encode path is a forecast; impact confidence is consequently capped below measured levels.
Local source evidence is unavailable at faiss/tests.
Local source evidence is unavailable at faiss/scalar_quantizer.*.

review_items.description: On the run host read /proc/cpuinfo or riscv_hwprobe and vlenb to confirm RVV availability and VLEN, and identify the core/microarchitecture before tuning LMUL.
Re-record with a higher sampling frequency or more benchmark iterations (perf record) and confirm the loop-body share before quantifying speedup.
Locate the sq-accuracy test source under faiss (tests or benchh) and confirm d, code_size, and the encode call path so the vectorization experimental setup matches the measured workload.
Implement the RVV encode prototype and A/B benchmark benchmark_QT_8bit_* against this scalar baseline on the target hardware.

alternative_explanations.explanation: Codegen shape (per-iteration this->d/vdiff reloads, base+i store addressing) rather than the missing vectorization could be claimed as the main cause, but the loop is short per iteration and the input pointer already uses addi a1,a1,4; the dominant fact is that all per-element work is scalar.

Only 11 cpu-clock samples were collected for the function, so the exact sample shares are statistically noisy; however every sampled address lies in the loaded/scalar loop or prologue, so the kind of bottleneck is not in doubt.

The scalar code is not caused by a build without vector support: the library ELF attribute string includes v1p0 with zvl128b/zve64d and the symbol name instantiates Codec8bit<RISCV_RVV>, and sq-rvv.cpp is compiled under COMPILE_SIMD_RISCV_RVV.

findings.conclusion: QuantizerTemplate<Codec8bit<RISCV_RVV>, QuantizerTemplateScaling::UNIFORM, SIMDLevel::NONE>::encode_vector runs a scalar per-component loop (disasm 0x7ac2a0-0x7ac2e6: flw x[i], fsub.s vmin, fdiv.s vdiff, two-sided clamp via flt.s+two bnez, fmul.s by 255, fcvt.w.s rtz, sb) with zero RVV instructions, although libfaiss.so is built with v1p0/zvl128b; the RISCV_RVV QuantizerTemplate in sq-rvv.cpp is a marker type that inherits the scalar NONE encode_vector, so QT_8bit uniform encoding never enters a vector path even though the operation is lane-independent contiguous elementwise arithmetic (7 of 11 annotate samples fall inside the loop body)

neighbor_exclusions.reason: Generic scalar-loop row acts as a fallback; this loop has proven lane independence and unit-stride contiguous accesses and the artifact is compiled with RVV, so the specific contiguous elementwise row owns the routing.
No specialized RVV encode kernel exists to be selected; the scalar fallback is the only implementation, so routing is the operator row rather than a selection/fallback row.
The fp->int conversion (fcvt.w.s) is a single small step; profile samples concentrate on compares, stores, and member loads, not on conversion handling.
vmin/vdiff are trained scalar broadcast parameters, not per-vector cross-lane statistics; there is no max/sum reduction pass.
No accumulation, reduction, or widening accumulator exists in the encode loop.

findings.reasoning: Direct disassembly of the target symbol shows only scalar F loads/computes/branches and a byte store; hotspots 0x7ac2cc flt.s 27.27%, 0x7ac2de sb 18.18%, 0x7ac2e2 ld 18.18% sit in the loop body. quantizers.h:66-90 defines the NONE encode_vector loop xi=(x[i]-vmin)/vdiff clamped to [0,1] then (int)(255*xi); sq-rvv.cpp:44-67 declares Codec8bit/QuantizerTemplate<..RISCV_RVV> as empty markers inheriting NONE, so no RVV encode exists. ELF attributes (ed49d3...) show the library was compiled with v1p0 and zvl128b, so the ISA gate is not the reason for the scalar code.

alternative_explanations.explanation: On an OoO core the reloads hit L1 (L1_dcache_load_miss_rate 0.317%) and may partly hide in latency windows, so their individual contribution is modest; they remain extra instructions and address arithmetic per component.

The reloads are a direct consequence of the scalar loop and disappear once RVV vectorization of encode_vector is added, so treating this as an independent avenue is optional and secondary to the root cause.

findings.conclusion: As long as the scalar codegen survives, the encode loop emits per-iteration overhead beyond the arithmetic: this->d is reloaded each iteration (ld a4,8(a0) at 0x7ac2e2), this->vdiff is reloaded (flw fa4,20(a0) at 0x7ac2a0) because the uint8_t* store to `code` forces a conservative aliasing assumption, and the byte-store address is recomputed as base+i (add a3,a2,a5) against a reloaded limit instead of pointer increments with a precomputed end pointer.

neighbor_exclusions.reason: Evidence is a limit reload and base+i recompute, not an i<n countdown comparison form; the loop already compares against the loaded limit register.
This is a loop-level induction-variable/limit reload issue, not a peephole algebraic identity inside a basic block.
No specialized encode kernel exists; the address-reload shape is inside the only implementation.

findings.reasoning: The disassembly shows the loop reloads both scalar members from `this` on every trip and recomputes the store address, while the float input pointer advances by addi a1,a1,4. quantizers.h encodes member access inside the loop body. These integer/load instructions are loop-invariant work that vectorization subsumes but that a scalar-only repair could remove.

asm.reason: Hot loop is compiler-generated scalar RISC-V (no vector or asm). No handwritten .S or policy-backed missing assembly kernel in this path; RISC-V SQ support in sq-rvv.cpp is C++ RVV intrinsics (marker Codec/Quantizer types + DCTemplate fast path), not assembly.

codegen.reason: Compiler-generated scalar loop exhibits per-iteration reloads of members (ld a4,8(a0); flw fa4,20(a0)), a serial fsub->fdiv->fcvt->sb dependency chain, and branchy clamp comparisons; candidate for codegen-shape and data-movement analysis.

crypto.reason: No cryptographic arithmetic, hash, checksum, or binary-field work; loop is plain float normalize/clamp/truncate-to-byte.

offload.reason: No GEMM, matrix-engine, or packed-SIMD offload opportunity; per-component affine quantize has no reduction structure.

operator_rvv.reason: Scalar per-component encode kernel xi=clip((x[i]-vmin)/vdiff,0,1); code[i]=(int)(255*xi) is lane-independent with a proven packed formulation (AVX2/NEON 8-wide decode; RVV intrinsics precedent in sq-rvv.cpp). 7/11 profile samples are inside this loop body.

runtime_os.reason: No timer, interrupt, privilege boundary, or runtime-context management in the hot loop.

string_memory.reason: Access pattern is trivial sequential float loads + byte stores; L1_dcache_load_miss_rate 0.317%, not memory-bound.

vectorized_tuning.reason: No compiler-generated RVV code in the target function at all; loop uses only scalar F instructions, so there is no existing vector code limited by configuration or bookkeeping.

summary.observed_anomaly: QuantizerTemplate<Codec8bit<RISCV_RVV>, QuantizerTemplateScaling::UNIFORM, SIMDLevel::NONE>::encode_vector runs a scalar per-component loop (disasm 0x7ac2a0-0x7ac2e6: flw x[i], fsub.s vmin, fdiv.s vdiff, two-sided clamp via flt.s+two bnez, fmul.s by 255, fcvt.w.s rtz, sb) with zero RVV instructions, although libfaiss.so is built with v1p0/zvl128b; the RISCV_RVV QuantizerTemplate in sq-rvv.cpp is a marker type that inherits the scalar NONE encode_vector, so QT_8bit uniform encoding never enters a vector path even though the operation is lane-independent contiguous elementwise arithmetic (7 of 11 annotate samples fall inside the loop body)
